title: Customer Cost-Sensitivity Allocator and Escalation Matrix for Optimization Requests
creator: Amira Soltan
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit optimization and advisory requests (batching/caching knob tuning, quant profiles, routing policies) with highly variable business impact. The current intake flow treats many signals equally, causing engineering toil on low-value asks and inconsistent SLA handling for high-impact customers.

Goal: Build a deterministic 'cost-sensitivity allocator' that scores incoming optimization requests across economic and risk dimensions, assigns them to a prioritization lane (self-serve, concierge, engineering triage), and provides an explicit escalation matrix when requests exceed a lane's remit. The allocator should be transparent to customers and ops: explain why a request was routed, what additional information is required, and expected SLA.

Scope: PM intake form changes, scoring rubric, admin override UI in Console, documentation for solutions/CS, and an initial implementation of automation rules for common cases (e.g., dedicated customers over $50k/mo; requests tagged latency-critical; requests affecting caching across >3 endpoints). We will not build automated tuning agents in this ticket — only the intake/routing logic and escalation paths.

Proposed solution (high level):
- Signals: monthly spend, deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private), SLA class, incident frequency, token volume, latency sensitivity flag, data-sensitivity / compliance tag, number of affected routes, historical churn.
- Scoring: weighted sum normalized 0-100. Weights are configurable per customer tier; default weights provided.
- Lanes: Self-serve (0-29), Concierge (30-59), Engineering Triage (60-84), Exec Escalation (85-100). Each lane has SLA targets and expected response actions.
- Escalation matrix: explicit triggers for auto-escalation (e.g., any request with weight on compliance=100 -> Engineering Triage), and human escalation guidelines for CS to push to Solutions or Sales.
- Outputs: assigned lane, estimated SLA (time to first response), recommended diagnostic artifacts (token traces, histograms, sample prompts), and a visibility tag for routing to Dedicated/Private specialists.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Automated scoring may surface false positives; include manual override and appeal flow.
- We want to start with conservative thresholds to avoid overloading Eng. Threshold tuning requires 6 weeks of telemetry.
- Implementation must work with existing Submit Optimizations flow in Console and be available as an API endpoint for partners and Support tools.

Success metrics: average time-to-first-response by lane, percent of engineering triage requests containing required artifacts, reduction in low-value eng work, CS satisfaction rating on routing accuracy.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form updated with new signal fields and help text for artifacts required
A scoring service (HTTP API) exists that returns lane, score, and reasoning string
Console admin page to view and override allocations for incoming requests
Escalation matrix doc published in Confluence with runbooks for each lane
Telemetry events emitted for score, lane, and override with schema agreed by analytics
Initial default weights and thresholds committed and feature-flagged for testing
updates: 2025-02-21: Kickoff meeting with Eng (Diego, Priya), Solutions (Maya), and CS (Oliver). Agreed signals and initial weight proposals.
2025-02-26: Engineering requested splitting 'latency sensitivity' into 'p99 SLA' and 'user-visible latency' to improve granularity. Added to signals list.
2025-02-28: Design (Rae) shared two intake prototypes: inline explainer vs sidebar score. Prefer inline for discoverability; Rae to iterate on visual affordances for overrides.
2025-03-03: Security reviewed initial plan; no additional controls needed but recommended logging for compliance-tagged requests. Marked as low lift.
2025-03-04: Analytics (Harper) requested telemetry keys and example events. Draft schema uploaded to Drive (link below).
2025-03-05: PM review: reduced default weights on 'monthly spend' to avoid promoting small but high-risk customers incorrectly. Preparing PRD for eng handoff.
notes: This ticket is intended to be the canonical PM artifact for the first-phase intake allocator. After rollout to internal CS and Solutions, we will open a 6-week telemetry window to tune thresholds. Consider follow-up projects: autoscorer integrations, dedicated-customer fast-path, and SLA-backed acceptance tests.
customer_examples: Large SaaS customer (dedicated, $120k/mo) requesting cache invalidation policy changes impacting 12 routes — expected lane: Engineering Triage
Mid-market customer (hosted, $8k/mo) asking for batching parameter guidance with sample prompts — expected lane: Concierge
Startup (hosted, low spend) looking for recommended quant profile to reduce inference cost — expected lane: Self-serve
